narrative.text: Morvec sends the invitation through a dockworker — no name, no address, just a warehouse number and a time. The port at night smells of salt and diesel and things being moved in the dark. He is already seated when you arrive, a ledger open on the table between two oil lamps.

I appreciate the discretion, Chancellor. The ledger details a cigarette operation — Lytheirian tobacco, Aldenmoor docks, no tariffs paid. The state loses perhaps ₭400,000 a year. I gain considerably more. What I am offering is a 20% share of the profit, routed through a holding account in your name. No state records. No campaign finance reports. Simply: money, in a place you need it.

He said it quietly, the way he says everything — as though the offer is a courtesy rather than a test. He already knows I need the campaign money. He already knows the treasury is strained. What he wants to find out is whether I know that accepting this makes me his, in a way that no formal arrangement ever has.

choices.text: Take the cut. The money is real and the need is real.
Refuse. 'I am not a partner in your operation, Stefan.'
Authorize Krel to raid the warehouse. End the operation tonight.

narrative.text: I told him yes. He closed the ledger, stood, and shook my hand — the grip of a man who has just concluded a business arrangement, not offered a bribe. The money appears in the holding account three days later. Clean. Untraceable. Useful. Every time I spend it I will know where it came from, and so will he.

He nodded once. No argument, no pressure — just the nod of a man filing the answer away. He closed the ledger. The operation continues without me. That is the part he wants me to understand: he doesn't need my permission. He was offering partnership, not asking for it. I refused. The warehouse keeps moving cigarettes. The treasury keeps losing ₭400,000 a year.

Krel moves within the hour. The warehouse is empty by the time his people arrive — Morvec's dockworkers cleared it in under twenty minutes, which means he knew I might do this. The ledger is gone. Three men are arrested who know nothing and say nothing. Morvec sends no message. He doesn't need to. I sat in his warehouse and then sent police to it. He will remember that the next time he decides what to offer me.
